name: Afimoxifene (4-hydroxytamoxifen)
lead: Afimoxifene, also called 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT), is an active metabolite of tamoxifen and a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM). It is an investigational drug, developed under the tentative brand name TamoGel as a topical gel for breast conditions [1].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding contexts it is discussed as a topical option for gynecomastia. Published trials of the gel have been in women, for cyclical breast pain (mastalgia), breast density and breast cancer settings; no trial in men with gynecomastia was identified [2][3].

paras: Afimoxifene acts on estrogen receptors alpha and beta, with estrogen-like or estrogen-blocking effects depending on tissue. It also binds the G protein-coupled estrogen receptor with much lower affinity than estradiol, and antagonises the estrogen-related receptors ERR-beta and ERR-gamma [1]. Its sulfation by human sulfotransferases, notably SULT1A1 and SULT1C4, has been characterised in lab work alongside endoxifen, raloxifene and fulvestrant [4].

The gel has been developed for breast hyperplasia and has completed a Phase II trial for cyclical mastalgia; Wikipedia notes more studies are needed before approval for that use [1]. Registered trials have also examined topical afimoxifene for mammographic breast density, ductal carcinoma in situ and in breast cancer survivors after radiation [5][6][7].

A Phase II randomised trial in premenopausal women compared two doses of 4-OHT gel with placebo gel for moderate to severe cyclical mastalgia; its stated aim was to assess safety and efficacy with a lower risk of the side effects associated with oral tamoxifen [2]. Further registered studies include a Phase III trial on mammographic density (terminated) [6], Phase II trials in DCIS [7], and a Phase II trial in women with dense breasts [5]. No studies in men with gynecomastia, and none on appearance outcomes, were found.

timeline.event: Phase II trial of afimoxifene gel in cyclical mastalgia begins [8].

card.summary: The active form of tamoxifen, studied as a breast gel in women; use for male gynecomastia has no published trials.

quick.overview:
Afimoxifene is the active metabolite of tamoxifen, formulated as a gel for application to the breast. It remains investigational.

Trials have been in women for breast pain, density and cancer settings. Its use for male gynecomastia, which is how it comes up in these communities, has not been tested in published trials found.
quick.mechanism: A SERM that blocks or mimics estrogen at estrogen receptors depending on the tissue; applied topically, the aim is local breast effects.
quick.risks: Not approved anywhere in the sources reviewed. Side-effect details for the gel were not reviewed in depth; the mastalgia trial was designed around avoiding the systemic effects of oral tamoxifen.
